instruction: Examine the spreadsheet on the desktop containing 2022 book reading records. Identify the author whose name appears first in the list. Write that author's full name in 'book_list_result.docx' on the desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires finding the first author in the list. Verified from Excel: George R. R. Martin is the author of the first book (Fire and Blood) in the list.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the instruction requirement: checks if the docx file contains the expected author name (George R. R. Martin)
Metric function correctly handles expected parameter - uses 'expected.get('expected_text')' directly (not 'expected.get('rules')')
Postconfig appropriately activates LibreOffice Writer window and saves the file with Ctrl+S to ensure file state is fresh
Expected value is semantically correct - metadata confirms 'George R. R. Martin' is the author of the first book in the list
Data flow is correct: get_vm_file retrieves docx → metric reads docx paragraphs → checks for expected text presence
Metric uses case-insensitive and fuzzy matching which is appropriate for text comparison with minor formatting variations
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The evaluator checks for text presence but doesn't verify the text was newly written vs pre-existing. However, this is acceptable given the workflow (file is downloaded initially, then modified and saved)
